transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well... I suppose I'm here because of an ongoing situation at my building. It's... well, for months now, the property manager and certain people in the building have been trying to pressure me out of my apartment. 

I wouldn't normally bring it up to a doctor, but it's been persistent. Just... subtle things. Misdelivered mail. Noises
Do you believe for certain that the property manager and other people in the building are deliberately trying to force you out?

Well... yes. I do. 

It's not really a matter of belief. You just... you look at the sequence of events. The misdelivered mail. The noises in the walls—which are timed, by the way. And... just little comments from the neighbors. 

They try to hand me paperwork or offer these everyday explanations, but... none of that changes the pattern I can clearly see. So, yes. I am certain.
Have you heard voices when no one is actually there?
No. No, I haven't. I just... I hear the noises I mentioned. The ones they make on purpose. But no, not voices.
If someone showed you clear proof that the property manager was not trying to force you out, would you be able to accept that?

I... I'm not sure what you mean by proof. 

I already told you. They hand me paperwork, they offer their explanations... but none of that changes the pattern I can clearly see. The mail, the noises... it's all still happening. 

So... no. A piece of paper wouldn't change what I know is going on.
Do you ever feel that someone can control your thoughts or put thoughts into your mind?

No. I... no. My thoughts are entirely my own. 

I don't really understand why you're asking me that. I'm just... observing what is actually happening in the building. No one is putting things in my head.
Have you ever felt that messages on TV, the radio, or the internet were meant specifically for you?

No. I... no, not at all. 

The television is just television. I don't really see what that has to do with my situation.
Has this situation made it hard for you to keep up with your usual daily activities?

I... well, yes. It takes up a lot of my time. 

I've had to pull back from a few consulting jobs recently. It's just... necessary. I spend most of the week having to follow up with neighbors, making calls to different offices, trying to get answers from the building staff. 

There isn't really time for my normal work right now. Or my painting. I just... I have to deal with this first.
About how long has this been going on?
I suppose... it's been about 11 months. Just... shortly after I moved into the new apartment. That's when it started.
Aside from what’s happening in your building, have you noticed your thoughts ever becoming jumbled or hard to organize?

No. I... no. My mind is perfectly clear. 

When I'm not forced to deal with the apartment situation, I'm as organized as ever. I manage my own finances, cook for myself, keep my appointments. If we were discussing my consulting work, or... or my painting, I could explain them to you without any issue. There is nothing wrong with my thoughts.
During this past year, have you had a period of feeling unusually depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?
No. I haven't. I... I don't get depressed. I'm just dealing with a stressful situation, that's all.
Do you think it is possible that you might be mistaken about the people in your building trying to force you out?

No. I... no, I don't. 

I analyze patterns for a living, Doctor. I know what I see. For months now, the property manager and... certain people in the building, they've been using specific tactics. Misdelivered mail. Noises in the walls that are timed perfectly. Little comments from the neighbors. 

They try to explain it away. They show me paperwork. But... no amount of their paperwork or explanations changes the pattern I can clearly see. They are trying to pressure me out of the apartment. I'm not mistaken about that.
During this past year, have you had a period of several days when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?
No. I... no. I sleep normally. I haven't experienced anything like that. I just stick to my usual routine.
Have you seen anything yourself that proves people in the building are doing this to you?

I... well, I don't have photographs or a confession, if that's what you mean. I just... I observe what happens around me. The things I already mentioned. I don't need to see a smoking gun to know what's going on.
Aside from the people in your building, do you believe anyone else is trying to harm, watch, or target you?
No. I... no. Just the people I mentioned. I don't have any reason to think anyone else is involved.
Have you found yourself caring much less than usual about seeing other people or doing things you normally enjoy?
No. I still care about the things I've always cared about. I just... I keep to myself a bit more now, given the circumstances. But I still enjoy my own interests.
Have you ever contacted the police or a lawyer about what you believe the people in your building are doing?
I haven't... no. I don't see what good that would do. I haven't contacted anyone like that.
Do you feel anxious or on edge most days because of this situation?
Not really. I wouldn't call it anxiety. I just... I stay aware of what's going on around me. That's all.
Before this started, had anything like this ever happened to you in any other place or with any other people?
No... no, nothing like this. It's just... here. With them. That's all.
Before this apartment situation began, did your ability to work and manage daily life change noticeably?

No. My ability to manage things hasn't changed. I... I still handle my finances just fine. I cook for myself, make it to my appointments. When I'm not forced to deal with the situation in the building, I'm perfectly organized. I can still talk about my consulting work, or my painting, without any issue. My daily life is fine.
